headline: The Senate blocked H.R. 3684, a large bill that would have funded roads, rail, broadband, water, energy, and other infrastructure, on July 21, 2021.
what_it_does: If adopted, this bill would have provided new federal funding and rules for many kinds of infrastructure, including roads, bridges, passenger and freight rail, public transit, broadband, ports, airports, water systems, the electric grid, and cleanup of old pollution sites. It would have reauthorized many transportation and safety programs through fiscal year 2026 and created new grant programs, such as for electric vehicle charging and wildlife crossings. It would also have included requirements on domestic sourcing of materials, prevailing wages on funded projects, and changes to drinking water, broadband, and energy programs. The Senate did not take up or end debate on the bill, so none of these changes were made.

who_it_affects.how: They would have received federal grants and loans for roads, bridges, transit, water systems, and broadband projects.
They would have seen funding for road and bridge repairs, highway safety programs, and new electric vehicle charging stations.

who_it_affects.group: People in rural and unserved areas
who_it_affects.how: They would have had access to broadband and middle mile internet grants, along with rural transit and ferry service funding.

who_it_affects.group: Users of Amtrak and passenger rail
who_it_affects.how: They would have benefited from grants for Amtrak service and a rule requiring a ticket agent at larger stations.
They would have faced new rules on automatic emergency braking for heavy trucks and an apprenticeship program for drivers under 21.
They would have received funding for tribal roads, bridges, water projects, and broadband.
They would have been eligible for an affordable broadband benefit and assistance with drinking water and wastewater connections.

who_it_affects.group: Coal communities and abandoned mine land areas
who_it_affects.how: They would have received funding to reclaim abandoned coal mines and to build clean energy manufacturing facilities.
They would have been subject to Buy American requirements for materials used in federally funded infrastructure projects.
